title: Evaluating the effectiveness of AI-generated, context-specific case studies in improving critical thinking skills in ODL
venue: American Journal of Advanced Technology and Engineering Solutions
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether AI-generated, context-specific case studies can improve critical thinking in open and distance learning (ODL) settings, compared with traditional instructor-developed case materials. The motivation is that static cases in ODL may lack contextual relevance, reduce engagement, and provide delayed or limited feedback, which can constrain development of higher-order thinking skills.

The study used a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test control group design with 200 learners in Bangladesh: 100 in an experimental group and 100 in a control group. Participants were drawn from Bangladesh Open University and selected private universities offering ODL or blended programs, and included students from education, business, and health sciences. The experimental group worked for six weeks with AI-generated case studies tailored to discipline, cultural background, and professional aspirations, with adaptive feedback embedded in the Moodle-based learning management system; the control group used static instructor-prepared cases.

Outcomes were measured using adapted critical thinking, engagement, authenticity, and feedback instruments, along with LMS analytics and reflective journals. The paper reports that the AI-based intervention produced substantially larger gains in critical thinking than the control condition, with significant effects associated with personalization, engagement, authenticity, and adaptive feedback. The author concludes that AI-generated case studies are a promising scalable scaffold for improving critical thinking in ODL, especially in contexts such as Bangladesh where access, equity, and contextualization are important concerns.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a quasi-experimental pre-test/post-test control group study with a defined comparison condition and reported statistical analyses, which is stronger than correlational evidence. However, it is not a randomized trial and relies on a single study in an ODL context, so some credibility concerns remain.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effect on critical thinking is large (d=0.85) and the intervention targets a priority population in ODL. The improvement over static case materials suggests meaningful educational impact rather than a marginal change.

interventions.use_case: AI-generated, context-specific case studies for ODL learners, with personalized scenarios and adaptive feedback delivered through an LMS to support critical thinking in case-based learning

finding.finding_summary: AI-generated, context-specific case studies produced substantial gains in critical thinking for the experimental group (n=100) compared with static instructor-prepared cases (n=100). Critical thinking on the CCTST increased from 18.4 to 25.7 in the experimental group versus 18.6 to 20.4 in the control group; the experimental group showed a large effect size (d=0.85, p<.001) and the control group a small effect size (d=0.22, p=.04).
finding.measure: California Critical Thinking Skills Test (CCTST) pre-test/post-test scores

finding.finding_summary: The intervention also improved learner engagement, which the paper treated as a key supporting outcome. The experimental group reported higher engagement (M=4.2/5) than the control group (M=3.1/5), and engagement correlated with critical thinking gains (r=.58 for skills engagement; r=.52 for emotional engagement); regression showed a positive effect on critical thinking (β=.39, p<.001).
finding.measure: Online Student Engagement Scale (OSE) and LMS analytics (time spent, forum contributions)
